A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-AU/CLIP-AUTT research. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials, including tables, figures and rendered equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on BioVid, StressID and BAH, including benchmark comparisons, subject-wise results, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds FERV39K evaluation, controlled ablations and repeated-seed performance estimates.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP encoders, AU adapter, temporal module, classifier, entropy-guided window selection and AU-embedding adaptation remain unchanged. Sentence-level prompts are tested as an ablation, rather than adopted as a revised method.

E1.justification: Supplementary Section 3.7(d) and Table 7(a) add FERV39K evaluation, extending coverage to common video FER beyond the retained BioVid, StressID and BAH settings. This is a focused additional benchmark.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables is unchanged. New comparisons reuse EmoCLIP and T3AL; SEV-Net motivates a prompt variant but is not evaluated as an additional baseline model.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce matched window-selection and full-frame controls for T3AL, every-Nth-frame sampling at intervals 2, 3, 5, 10 and 25, and matched training/testing prompt styles. The original subject splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Main Table 5 newly isolates window selection and AU tuning. Supplementary Section 3.7 adds matched-window/full-video comparisons, sampling-rate sensitivity and phrase-versus-sentence prompt ablations. Main Figure 5 adds a temporal-selection case study. Together these substantially expand component attribution and robustness analysis beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: v3 reports StressID performance means and standard deviations over three random seeds for T3AL and CLIP-AUTT in supplementary Figure 5. v1 provides no corresponding seed-based performance uncertainty. This addition is limited to two methods on one dataset; no significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and subject-wise scores remain unchanged, but substantial new findings are reported. FERV39K results include CLIP-AUTT at 51.1 WAR/44.7 F1 versus T3AL at 43.8/38.1. Main Table 5 adds window-only results of 78.7/75.2 and tuning-only results of 80.0/76.4. Further new results cover seeds, sampling and prompt styles; these are additions, not improvements to existing same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, main Equations 1–13 and supplementary entropy-gradient explanation are unchanged when checked visually. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about AU-guided alignment and subject-specific test-time adaptation. The added efficiency sentence makes the existing Figure 1 comparison explicit without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets AU tuning as the larger component contributor, argues that gains persist beyond window-selection advantages, and attributes better phrase-level performance to cleaner localized semantic anchors. It also discusses generalization to common FER and possible alignment confounds from alternative video encoders. Existing BAH limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1's statement that code will be made public is replaced by an explicit repository link, and v3 adds a project-page link. These are documented access improvements; external availability was not checked. Existing hardware, optimizer, batch-size and adaptation-budget disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Supplementary Section 3.7(e) newly relates sentence-level AU prompts to SEV-Net. Otherwise, research positioning is retained; updates to MUSACO and other references concern publication metadata rather than newly cited research.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and front-matter edits, adds acknowledgments, and replaces the appendix's qualitative-discussion subsection with Additional Analysis of CLIP-AUTT. The main section sequence and most existing explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The results displays are substantially reorganized and expanded. v1's mixed Figure 4 is separated into qualitative Figure 4 and Table 4, with the fuller appendix qualitative panel moved into the main text. New displays include the temporal-window example, component table, uncertainty/control panels, sampling plot and FERV39K/prompt comparisons.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct controls separating the two adaptation components and testing whether baseline input selection explained the gains. v3's main Table 5 and supplementary Section 3.7 address these important evidential gaps, while three-seed estimates strengthen the stability evidence. FERV39K protocol details remain sparse, limiting that extension's reproducibility, but the added controls substantially strengthen support for the unchanged method.
